ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=8$, $BC=4\sqrt{7}$. A circle with center O on side BC is drawn to be tangent to AB and AC at D and E, respectively. What is the length of AD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Join $AO$, $OD$, and $OB$.\\
Since $AB$ and $AC$ are tangent to point $D$ and $E$, respectively,\\
it follows that $OD\perp AB$ and $OE\perp AC$,\\
and since $AO=AO$,\\
it results in $\triangle ADO \cong \triangle AEO$ (by Hypotenuse-Leg),\\
thus $\angle DAO = \angle EAO$,\\
and since $AB=AC$,\\
it follows that $AO \perp BC$ and $BO=OC=2\sqrt{7}$,\\
by applying the Pythagorean theorem we get\\
$AO=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BO^{2}}=6$,\\
since $\angle DAO = \angle BAO$ and $\angle ADO = \angle AOB$,\\
it results in $\triangle ADO \sim \triangle AOB$,\\
thus $\frac{AD}{AO} = \frac{AO}{AB}$,\\
therefore, $AD=\boxed{\frac{9}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows an isosceles triangle ABC, with vertex A above, and B and C at the two ends of the horizontal base below; the center O of a circle is marked on the base BC. The circle is tangent to sides AB and AC respectively, and the points of tangency are marked as D and E, where D is on AB and E is on AC. Reasoning: Connect AO, OD, OB. Because the circle is tangent to AB and AC respectively at D and E, the radius OD ⟂ AB, OE ⟂ AC. The distances from O to the two sides AB and AC of angle A are equal, therefore AO bisects ∠A. Also because AB = AC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, so the angle bisector AO drawn from A is also perpendicular to and bisects BC, therefore BO = OC = BC/2 = 2√7, and AO ⟂ BC. In right triangle AOB, AB = 8, BO = 2√7, so AO = √(AB² - BO²) = √(64 - 28) = √36 = 6. Then compare the right triangles ADO and AOB: ∠ADO = 90°, ∠AOB = 90°; and AD is on AB, so ∠DAO and ∠OAB are the same angle. Therefore △ADO ∼ △AOB. The correspondence gives AD/AO = AO/AB, so AD = AO²/AB = 6²/8 = 36/8 = 9/2.
